title: Ratio and proportion
ks3: Ratio, proportion and rates of change: ratio, sharing, direct and inverse proportion, scales
intro: Mixing drinks, sharing sweets, scaling recipes and reading maps. Practise ratios, sharing in a ratio, proportion and scale.
description: Free KS3 Maths ratio and proportion questions with answers: simplifying ratios, sharing in a ratio, recipes, best buys, inverse proportion and map scales. Marked instantly, for Year 7, 8 and 9 (ages 9 to 14).

questions.q: A bag has 3 red sweets and 5 blue sweets. What is the ratio of red to blue?
questions.hint: Write red first, because the question says "red to blue".
questions.explain: There are 3 red and 5 blue, so red : blue = 3 : 5.

questions.q: Which ratio is the same as 1 : 4?
questions.hint: Multiply both parts by the same number.
questions.explain: 1 : 4 multiplied by 3 is 3 : 12. (2 : 6 is the same as 1 : 3.)

questions.q: Simplify the ratio 6 : 9
questions.hint: Divide both parts by the biggest number that goes into both.
questions.explain: Divide both by 3: 6 : 9 = 2 : 3.

questions.q: Simplify the ratio 20 : 35 : 15
questions.hint: 5 goes into all three numbers.
questions.explain: Divide all three parts by 5: 20 : 35 : 15 = 4 : 7 : 3.

questions.q: A drink is made with squash and water in the ratio 2 : 3. What fraction of the drink is squash?
questions.hint: How many parts are there altogether?
questions.explain: There are 2 + 3 = 5 parts and 2 of them are squash, so {2/5} of the drink is squash.

questions.q: A pet shop has 4 cats and 10 dogs. What is the ratio of dogs to cats, in its simplest form?
questions.hint: Dogs come first. Then divide both numbers by the same number.
questions.explain: Dogs to cats is 10 : 4. Divide both by 2 to get 5 : 2.

questions.q: Write the ratio 50p : £2 in its simplest form.
questions.hint: Change both amounts into pence first.
questions.explain: £2 = 200p, so the ratio is 50 : 200. Divide both by 50 to get 1 : 4.

questions.q: Write the ratio 4 : 10 in the form 1 : n.
questions.hint: To make the first number 1, divide both numbers by 4.
questions.explain: Divide both sides by 4: 4 ÷ 4 = 1 and 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5. So 4 : 10 = 1 : 2.5.

questions.q: Share £30 in the ratio 1 : 2. How much is the bigger share, in pounds?
questions.hint: How many parts altogether? How much is one part worth?
questions.explain: 1 + 2 = 3 parts. One part = £30 ÷ 3 = £10. The bigger share is 2 parts = £20.

questions.q: Squash and water are mixed in the ratio 2 : 3. How much water is needed for 100 ml of squash?
questions.hint: 2 parts are 100 ml. How much is 1 part?
questions.explain: 2 parts = 100 ml, so 1 part = 50 ml. Water is 3 parts = 150 ml.

questions.q: Ann and Bo share 48 sweets in the ratio 5 : 3. How many sweets does Ann get?
questions.hint: 5 + 3 = 8 parts. Find one part first.
questions.explain: One part = 48 ÷ 8 = 6 sweets. Ann gets 5 × 6 = 30 and Bo gets 3 × 6 = 18.

questions.q: The ratio of boys to girls in a club is 4 : 5. There are 20 boys. How many children are in the club altogether?
questions.hint: 4 parts are 20 boys. How many is one part?
questions.explain: 4 parts = 20, so one part = 5. Girls = 5 × 5 = 25. Altogether 20 + 25 = 45 children.

questions.q: Share 20 sweets in the ratio 1 : 4. How many sweets are in the smaller share?
questions.hint: How many parts are there altogether?
questions.explain: 1 + 4 = 5 parts. One part = 20 ÷ 5 = 4 sweets. The smaller share is 1 part, which is 4 sweets.

questions.q: Tom and Ella share £45 in the ratio 4 : 5. How much does Ella get, in pounds?
questions.hint: Add the parts, then find what one part is worth.
questions.explain: 4 + 5 = 9 parts. One part = £45 ÷ 9 = £5. Ella gets 5 parts = 5 × £5 = £25.

questions.q: A bracelet has red, blue and green beads in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5. There are 60 beads. How many beads are blue?
questions.hint: There are 2 + 3 + 5 parts. Find one part first.
questions.explain: 2 + 3 + 5 = 10 parts. One part = 60 ÷ 10 = 6 beads. Blue is 3 parts = 3 × 6 = 18 beads.

questions.q: Sam and Kai share some money in the ratio 3 : 7. Kai gets £24 more than Sam. How much does Sam get, in pounds?
questions.hint: How many more parts does Kai have than Sam? Those parts are worth £24.
questions.explain: Kai has 7 − 3 = 4 more parts than Sam, and 4 parts = £24, so 1 part = £6. Sam gets 3 parts = 3 × £6 = £18. (Check: Kai gets £42, and £42 − £18 = £24.)

questions.q: 3 pencils cost 60p. How much do 5 pencils cost, in pence?
questions.hint: Find the cost of 1 pencil first.
questions.explain: 1 pencil costs 60 ÷ 3 = 20p. 5 pencils cost 5 × 20 = 100p (£1).

questions.q: A recipe for 4 people uses 200 g of flour. How much flour is needed for 6 people?
questions.hint: Work out the flour for 1 person, or for 2 people.
questions.explain: For 2 people you need 100 g, so for 6 people you need 3 × 100 = 300 g.

questions.q: Which is better value?
questions.hint: Work out the cost of 100 g for each.
questions.explain: 500 g for £2.00 is 40p per 100 g. 200 g for £1.00 is 50p per 100 g. So the 500 g pack is better value.

questions.q: 4 painters take 6 hours to paint a fence. How long would 3 painters take, working at the same speed?
questions.hint: Fewer painters take longer. How long would 1 painter take?
questions.explain: 1 painter would take 4 × 6 = 24 hours. 3 painters take 24 ÷ 3 = 8 hours. This is inverse proportion.

questions.q: A tap fills a 12-litre bucket in 3 minutes. How long does it take to fill a 20-litre bucket?
questions.hint: How many litres does the tap fill each minute?
questions.explain: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 litres per minute. 20 ÷ 4 = 5 minutes.

questions.q: 5 apples cost £1.50. How much does 1 apple cost, in pence?
questions.hint: Change £1.50 into pence, then divide by 5.

questions.q: Which pack of dog treats is better value?
questions.hint: Work out the cost of one treat in each pack.
questions.explain: £3.00 ÷ 12 = 25p per treat. £2.40 ÷ 8 = 30p per treat. 25p is cheaper, so the pack of 12 is better value.

questions.q: A recipe for 12 cupcakes uses 150 g of butter. How much butter is needed for 30 cupcakes?
questions.hint: Find the butter for 6 cupcakes first (half of the recipe). How many lots of 6 make 30?
questions.explain: 6 cupcakes need 150 ÷ 2 = 75 g. 30 cupcakes is 5 lots of 6, so 5 × 75 = 375 g.

questions.q: A map has a scale of 1 : 50,000. Two places are 2 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they in real life, in kilometres?
questions.hint: 1 cm on the map is 50,000 cm in real life. 100,000 cm = 1 km.

questions.q: A model car is made to a scale of 1 : 20. The model is 21 cm long. How long is the real car, in metres?
questions.hint: The real car is 20 times as long.

questions.q: On a map, 1 cm stands for 5 km. Two towns are 3 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they in real life?
questions.hint: Each centimetre on the map is 5 km in real life.
questions.explain: 3 × 5 = 15, so the towns are 15 km apart.

questions.q: A map has a scale of 1 : 25,000. A real path is 1.5 km long. How long is the path on the map, in centimetres?
questions.hint: Change 1.5 km into centimetres first (1 km = 100,000 cm), then divide by 25,000.
